text:
maya-r: quick sync — I'm proposing we stop implicit project fallback at the gateway level. If a request lacks `X-Project-Id` we should return 428 Precondition Required (instead of silently falling back to org default). Reason: subtle cost/accounting and security surprises. Thoughts?

alex.m: +1 on making it explicit. Do we add a temporary opt-in header to preserve old behaviour for customers during rotation?

kevin_dev: question — why 428 instead of 400/401/403? 428 signals client precondition (header) missing which seems clearer than 401. Also helps SDKs to surface a clear remediation.

maya-r: exactly. 401/403 are ambiguous (auth vs permissions). 400 feels generic. 428 lets us say: "project header required; include X-Project-Id or add ?allow_implicit_project=true during migration".

tanvi: agree with 428. Two asks: 1) add `WWW-Authenticate` header with an error code so browsers/clients can surface guided UX. 2) add a telemetry counter `auth.missing_project_header`.

alex.m: minor nit: we should define exact JSON error contract so SDKs can auto-handle. Proposal: `{\n  \"error\": \"missing_project_id\",\n  \"message\": \"X-Project-Id header required\",\n  \"hint\": \"set X-Project-Id or add query param allow_implicit_project=true for legacy clients\"\n}`

kevin_dev: +1. And include `WWW-Authenticate: Project realm=\"redwood\", error=\"missing_project_id\"` for non-JSON clients.

ops-bot: deploy-check: gateway config change will require rollout window and smoke tests. Flags: `require_project_header` boolean, `migration_allowlist` for org IDs.

maya-r: here's a quick curl example of proposed response (for docs):

```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 428 Precondition Required
Content-Type: application/json
WWW-Authenticate: Project realm=\"redwood\", error=\"missing_project_id\"

{
  "error": "missing_project_id",
  "message": "X-Project-Id header required",
  "hint": "set X-Project-Id or use ?allow_implicit_project=true during migration"
}
```

tanvi: for SDKs: surface a dedicated exception type `MissingProjectHeaderError` and a helper that can attach org default if user enables migration mode. We'll put a deprecation notice in SDK v2.4.0.

alex.m: logging: tag spans with `auth.missing_project_header=true` and include `client_id` if available. Also create onboarding doc for partner infra teams (proxy config often strips custom headers).

kevin_dev: rotation/keys question: if a rotated key maps to a different org that requires explicit project id, should we still return 428? I think yes — header is orthogonal to key validity. Invalid key => 401; missing project header => 428; key lacking project access => 403.

maya-r: agreed — keep semantics strict: 401 invalid/malformed key, 403 authn succeeded but not authorized for requested project, 428 missing required header. We'll add a small decision table to the API contract doc.

ci-bot: build/test results for gateway branch `require-project-header`: all unit tests passed, integration tests: 2 failures related to test proxies (flaky). See CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/4203

ops-bot: deployment plan: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours, monitor `auth.missing_project_header` and `errors.428_rate`. Rollback if 428 spike > baseline + 5 sigma.

maya-r: action items: 1) @kevin_dev open gateway PR to return 428 + WWW-Authenticate + JSON body (include migration allowlist) 2) @tanvi update SDKs to surface error and add opt-in helper 3) @alex.m docs + proxy checklist 4) ops to schedule canary next Tue. I'll open a short RFC and link PRs.

alex.m: ping me on the PR for review, I'll add the error contract to the OpenAPI spec.

kevin_dev: will do, PR by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
